modules.notes: Real two-leg check, but it cannot reach CONFIRMED here. The leg that fires on a shipped workspace is the registration one: the display name is chosen at registration and the verification mail goes to an address nobody proved ownership of. A module must not post to a registration route (it would create an account on a deployment the operator does not own), so this module drives the reset leg instead, and that leg does not carry the name under the shipped Forgot_Password_Email template: verified against this lab, the recovery mail for an account whose display name is the attacker's sentence does not contain it. Supply RECIPIENT and MARKER from a registration you performed yourself, or drive the whole thing with the finding's automation.py.

notes: Every CONFIRMED finding in exploits/index.json is server-side, so skipped is empty: all 57 have an auxiliary scanner and an exploit module. None of them gives code execution, so no module is an exploit that opens a session; each finding's exploit module is an auxiliary/gather (it reads what the bug discloses) or an auxiliary/admin (it performs the action the bug allows). Modules were linted with the framework's own msftidy and run against the live lab on 127.0.0.1:39649, both inside the attacker container, one msfconsole invocation per module, and each one was also run against a route that is not vulnerable; the verdicts in validation are read from those transcripts with det.parse_msf_run. msftidy's RuboCop step cannot run on a standalone module outside the framework's git tree, so its format checks are what 'clean' reports, with that caveat recorded. The lab was provisioned host-side before the runs, by the operator and never by a module: a private room with a protected upload and a member banned from it, pending media ids, a revoked incoming-integration credential whose post-as role was granted manage-own-outgoing-integrations (the condition VULN-019 records), an Omnichannel agent and a visitor with page history, an account whose display name carries attacker prose, and a configured OAuth service. work/16/provision_b.py and provision_b2.py are those steps. A NEEDS_MANUAL module is correct, loaded and linted, and names what it needs: a DDP websocket client for the six realtime findings (stream-notify-room is a publication, not a method, so the DDP-over-REST bridge cannot carry it, verified against the lab), an identity provider for the four OAuth findings, a live second-factor code, an out-of-band listener, or a trigger route a module must not post to.
